motifs.name: local stone density territory
motifs.description: Empty points whose surrounding 7x7 neighborhood holds at least two more own than enemy stones count as own territory in a komi-adjusted area estimate.

motifs.name: decay influence territory
motifs.description: Each empty point goes to the side whose distance-decayed influence from stones within Manhattan distance four is clearly larger, and the evaluated side leads the resulting komi-adjusted area estimate.

motifs.name: power border territory
motifs.description: Each connected empty region is owned by the side whose bordering stones have more group-liberty weight (capped at six) with a margin, and the evaluated side leads the resulting komi-adjusted area estimate.

motifs.name: besieged group imbalance
motifs.description: The opponent has more stones in groups that are in atari, down to two liberties, or fully surrounded by enemy stones than the evaluated side does.

motifs.name: favorable contact fights
motifs.description: Along each boundary between an evaluated-side group and an opponent group where at least one side has under six liberties, the evaluated side more often holds the liberty lead.

motifs.name: locally outnumbered stone imbalance
motifs.description: Stones whose surrounding 3x3 neighborhood contains at least two more enemy stones than friendly stones are locally overwhelmed, and the opponent has clearly more such overwhelmed stones than the evaluated side.

motifs.name: capture ledger advantage
motifs.description: Because players alternate moves, a surplus of evaluated-side stones on the board means the evaluated side has captured more enemy stones than it has lost, and a clearly positive capture ledger favors the evaluated side.

motifs.name: strong cutting stones advantage
motifs.description: Stones belonging to groups with at least four liberties that touch two or more separate enemy groups are powerful cutting stones, and the evaluated side has more of them than the opponent.

motifs.name: isolated fighting stones imbalance
motifs.description: A stone with no friendly stone anywhere in its 3x3 neighborhood but at least one enemy stone within Manhattan distance two is a stranded fighting stone, and the opponent has clearly more such stranded stones than the evaluated side.

motifs.name: head hit pressure advantage
motifs.description: An own stone placed directly in front of an enemy line of two or more stones strikes its head and blocks its advance, a powerful attacking shape, and the evaluated side lands clearly more of these head hits (with longer blocked runs counting double) than the opponent.

motifs.name: strength mismatch pressure
motifs.description: Stones in groups with at most three liberties that sit next to an enemy group with five or more liberties are crushed by superior force, and the opponent having clearly more such overmatched stones than the evaluated side signals a winning fight balance.

motifs.name: pressed low line stones imbalance
motifs.description: A stone stuck on the first or second line with an enemy stone directly inward is crawling low, an inefficient shape that yields little territory, and the opponent owning clearly more such pressed-low stones than the evaluated side signals a good exchange.

motifs.name: secure center weight advantage
motifs.description: Stones near the board center in groups with at least three liberties radiate influence, and a clearly larger center-weighted tally of such secure stones for the evaluated side signals control of the middle game.

motifs.name: empty triangle inefficiency imbalance
motifs.description: A 2x2 block containing exactly three stones of one color plus one empty point is an inefficient empty-triangle shape, and the opponent forms clearly more of these bad shapes than the evaluated side.

motifs.name: capture weighted area
motifs.description: Groups in atari or with at most three liberties touching only one tiny empty region are treated as captured, and the evaluated side leads a komi-adjusted area estimate counting sealed regions (ignoring dead stones) plus double the dead-stone swing.

motifs.name: netted stone imbalance
motifs.description: A stone is netted when no ray from it reaches friendly reinforcements or an open lane of four empty points while at least three of its four rays quickly hit enemy stones, meaning it is trapped inside a loose enemy net even with nearby space, and the opponent having clearly more netted stones than the evaluated side signals successful encirclement.

motifs.name: ray enclosure territory
motifs.description: Empty points whose nearest stones along the four orthogonal rays include at least two evaluated-side stones and no opponent stone count as enclosed territory, and the evaluated side leads in such points after komi.

motifs.name: swarmed group imbalance
motifs.description: The opponent has more stones in groups whose surrounding ring of stones is numerically dominated by the evaluated side than the evaluated side does in opponent-dominated rings.
motifs.source:
MOTIF_NAME = 'swarmed group imbalance'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'The opponent has more stones in groups whose surrounding ring of stones is numerically dominated by the evaluated side than the evaluated side does in opponent-dominated rings.'

def motif(board_rows: list[str], color: str) -> bool:
    br = board_rows
    gid = [-1] * 361
    gsize = []
    gcol = []
    gcells = []
    for r in range(19):
        for c in range(19):
            i = r * 19 + c
            s = br[r][c]
            if s == '.' or gid[i] >= 0:
                continue
            g = len(gsize)
            gid[i] = g
            cl = []
            st = [i]
            while st:
                x = st.pop()
                cl.append(x)
                rr = x // 19
                cc = x - rr * 19
                for k in (-19 if rr else 0, 19 if rr < 18 else 0, -1 if cc else 0, 1 if cc < 18 else 0):
                    if k:
                        y = x + k
                        if br[y // 19][y % 19] == s and gid[y] < 0:
                            gid[y] = g
                            st.append(y)
            gsize.append(len(cl))
            gcol.append(s)
            gcells.append(cl)
    own_sw = 0
    opp_sw = 0
    for g in range(len(gsize)):
        s = gcol[g]
        e = 'W' if s == 'B' else 'B'
        fr = set()
        fo = set()
        for x in gcells[g]:
            rr = x // 19
            cc = x - rr * 19
            r0 = rr - 1 if rr else 0
            r1 = rr + 2 if rr < 18 else 19
            c0 = cc - 1 if cc else 0
            c1 = cc + 2 if cc < 18 else 19
            for r2 in range(r0, r1):
                row = br[r2]
                for c2 in range(c0, c1):
                    y = r2 * 19 + c2
                    t = row[c2]
                    if t == e:
                        fo.add(y)
                    elif t == s and gid[y] != g:
                        fr.add(y)
        if len(fo) >= 3 and len(fo) - len(fr) >= 2:
            if s == color:
                own_sw += gsize[g]
            else:
                opp_sw += gsize[g]
    return opp_sw - own_sw >= 4

motifs.name: corner stronghold advantage
motifs.description: Each 5x5 corner region where a side has at least two stones and at least two more than the opponent is a secured corner, and owning more corners than the opponent signals a winning territorial foundation.

motifs.name: enclosed swing area advantage
motifs.description: Flood-filling all points not held by a side and keeping only the components sealed off from the board edge gives that side fully enclosed area where enemy stones inside count as captured swing, and the evaluated side is winning when its stone count plus twice its enclosed area clearly exceeds the opponent's.

motifs.name: poisoned entry points advantage
motifs.description: An empty point is poisoned for a side when playing there would be suicide or immediate atari without capturing (eyes, tiger mouths, hopeless extensions), and the opponent faces clearly more such poisoned points than the evaluated side.

motifs.name: miai connected stones advantage
motifs.description: Two same-color groups sharing at least two different liberties cannot be cut apart (miai connection), and the evaluated side has clearly more stones in such securely linked groups than the opponent.

motifs.name: spread fighting groups advantage
motifs.description: Counting connected groups of two or more stones for each side, the evaluated side fields at least three more such groups than the opponent, indicating broadly spread living forces rather than a few clumped lumps.
motifs.source:
MOTIF_NAME = 'spread fighting groups advantage'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'Counting connected groups of two or more stones for each side, the evaluated side fields at least three more such groups than the opponent, indicating broadly spread living forces rather than a few clumped lumps.'

def motif(board_rows: list[str], color: str) -> bool:
    br = board_rows
    gid = [-1] * 361
    gsize = []
    gcol = []
    for r in range(19):
        for c in range(19):
            i = r * 19 + c
            s = br[r][c]
            if s == '.' or gid[i] >= 0:
                continue
            g = len(gsize)
            gid[i] = g
            st = [i]
            n = 0
            while st:
                x = st.pop()
                n += 1
                rr = x // 19
                cc = x - rr * 19
                if rr and gid[x - 19] < 0 and br[rr - 1][cc] == s:
                    gid[x - 19] = g
                    st.append(x - 19)
                if rr < 18 and gid[x + 19] < 0 and br[rr + 1][cc] == s:
                    gid[x + 19] = g
                    st.append(x + 19)
                if cc and gid[x - 1] < 0 and br[rr][cc - 1] == s:
                    gid[x - 1] = g
                    st.append(x - 1)
                if cc < 18 and gid[x + 1] < 0 and br[rr][cc + 1] == s:
                    gid[x + 1] = g
                    st.append(x + 1)
            gsize.append(n)
            gcol.append(s)
    own_g = 0
    opp_g = 0
    for g in range(len(gsize)):
        if gsize[g] >= 2:
            if gcol[g] == color:
                own_g += 1
            else:
                opp_g += 1
    return own_g - opp_g >= 3

motifs.name: large endangered group imbalance
motifs.description: Stones in groups of four or more with at most three liberties are in danger of being captured, and the opponent has clearly more such endangered stones than the evaluated side.

motifs.name: double strike tactical points
motifs.description: An empty point is a double strike for a side when playing there would be legal and would capture or put in atari two or more different enemy groups, and the evaluated side holds clearly more such double-strike points than the opponent.

motifs.name: clean pocket territory
motifs.description: Empty points whose 3x3 neighborhood holds at least two evaluated-side stones and no opponent stone mark uncontested space, and the evaluated side leads in such points after komi.

motifs.name: confined group imbalance
motifs.description: The opponent has more stones in groups that touch no empty region larger than three points and thus lack room for eyes or escape.

motifs.name: sector stone dominance
motifs.description: The board is split into nine sectors by thirds along each axis; a side owns a sector when it has at least three stones there and at least two more than the opponent, and controlling at least two more sectors than the opponent signals overall board dominance.

motifs.name: eye point imbalance
motifs.description: Empty points whose in-board orthogonal neighbors are all stones of one side are eye points, and the evaluated side has at least two more such eye points than the opponent.

motifs.name: tiger mouth shape advantage
motifs.description: An empty interior point with exactly three orthogonal neighbors of one color and the fourth orthogonal neighbor empty is a tiger mouth, a strong flexible shape for both attack and defense, and the evaluated side forms clearly more tiger mouths than the opponent.
